review_notes: I read the whole file and the `trade`, `key_trade` and `leftSet_trade` definitions in PairFiber.lean. I also read the uses of `stateFiberEquiv`, `trade_original` and `leftSet_trade` in other SwitchChain files (PairEqualitySlice, PairCrossToggleTransport, PairSwapFlipProjection, PairFiberTransport). The finding below is the only well-supported one. The existing simp lemmas `*_apply` and `*_symm_apply` are rfl lemmas with `Subtype.val` on the left. They look well-oriented and I saw no loop risk. `trade_original` is only ever applied with `exact`, so I did not recommend a simp attribute for it. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemma is untested.

findings.excerpt:
((stateFiberEquiv G i j hij).symm T).val.val =
      trade G.val i j hij T.val T.property.1 := rfl
findings.problem: The simp set unfolds `(stateFiberEquiv ..).symm T` into a raw `trade ..` term. Neither `leftSet_trade` nor `key_trade` is a simp lemma. So `simp` cannot reduce the canonical goal `leftSet ((stateFiberEquiv G i j hij).symm T).val.val i j`, which is the main fact about this equivalence, back to `T.val`. After the simp rewrite the term is stuck in `trade`. Downstream proofs therefore have to spell out `rw [stateFiberEquiv_symm_apply, leftSet_trade, ...]`. The same two-step rewrite appears in PairEqualitySlice (`observable_reconstruction`) and in PairCrossToggleTransport (`fiberSwapEquiv_leftSet`). PairFiberTransport also adds `stateFiberEquiv_symm_leftSet`, which is just `symm_apply_apply` restated by hand.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a simp lemma next to the `symm_apply` lemmas, stated on the equivalence side. For example:
`@[simp] theorem leftSet_stateFiberEquiv_symm ... (T : Assignment G.val i j) : leftSet ((stateFiberEquiv G i j hij).symm T).val.val i j = T.val := leftSet_trade G.val i j hij T.val T.property.1`.
Add the analogue for `graphFiberEquiv`, `leftSet ((graphFiberEquiv G i j hij).symm T).val i j = T.val`. Optionally add `key i j ((stateFiberEquiv G i j hij).symm T).val.val = key i j G.val`, whose proof is `key_trade ..`.
Because these are stated on the `.symm` form, they should fire before `stateFiberEquiv_symm_apply` unfolds to `trade`. Also check that the unfolding lemma does not pre-empt them. If it does, state the lemma with `trade` on the left, or give it higher priority.
findings.benefit: Goals mentioning `leftSet` of a reconstructed graph close with `simp`. The manual `rw [stateFiberEquiv_symm_apply, leftSet_trade]` sequences disappear from proofs such as `observable_reconstruction` and `fiberSwapEquiv_leftSet`. A reader no longer has to remember to apply `leftSet_trade` after unfolding.
